t: Automated Patent and Technical Literature Analyzer — Overview and definition

body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Mines patents and papers for prior art, trends, and white space. A patent and literature analyzer ingests patent full text and papers, extracts claims and concepts, maps citation networks, and finds prior art and white space. Real implementations use USPTO/Google Patents APIs with NLP pipelines and tools like PatSnap. It produces claim charts and freedom-to-operate heat maps.

title: Automated Patent and Technical Literature Analyzer — Teaching-ladder exercise
t: Automated Patent and Technical Literature Analyzer — Teaching-ladder exercise
description: Mines patents and papers for prior art, trends, and white space.
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Teaching ladder for Automated Patent and Technical Literature Analyzer, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Full-text patent and paper ingestion). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Full-text patent and paper ingestion and Claim parsing and concept extraction. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Engineering knowledge and reference search engine) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
